# Sirach Chapter 35 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 35 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 35 presents Ben Sira's theology of sacrifice: ethical obedience is itself the best offering (vv. 1–3), but this does not eliminate material sacrifice — it must be wholehearted and honest (vv. 4–10). The chapter then pivots to divine impartiality (v. 11b: "with him there is no partiality") and God's special attention to the widow, orphan, and wronged poor (vv. 12–14). The climax (vv. 16–20) is a powerful eschatological prayer for God's justice against oppressors. Verse 11 contains one of the chapter's most quoted phrases; "the Lord is judge, and with him there is no partiality" should be rendered with full weight. Note that the chapter has only 20 verses in Vaticanus (some versifications count differently).

---

35:1 Whoever keeps the law multiplies offerings; whoever heeds the commandments sacrifices a peace offering.

35:2 Whoever returns a kindness offers fine flour; whoever gives to charity offers a thank offering.

35:3 To refrain from evil is pleasing to the Lord, and to abstain from injustice is an atonement.

35:4 Do not come before the Lord empty-handed, for all these things are in fulfillment of the commandment.

35:5 The offering of the righteous enriches the altar, and its pleasing aroma rises before the Most High.

35:6 The sacrifice of a righteous person is acceptable, and its memorial will never be forgotten.

35:7 Honor the Lord with generosity, and do not reduce the firstfruits of your hands.

35:8 With every offering show a cheerful face, and dedicate your tithe with gladness.

35:9 Give to the Most High as he has given you — generously, according to your means.

35:10 For the Lord is one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.

35:11 Do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it; and do not trust in a dishonest sacrifice; for the Lord is the judge, and with him there is no partiality.

35:12 He will not show partiality against the poor, and he hears the prayer of the one who is wronged.

35:13 He will not disregard the petition of the orphan, nor the widow when she pours out her complaint.

35:14 Do not the widow's tears run down her cheek? And is not her cry against the one who caused them to fall?

35:15 Whoever serves God wholeheartedly will be accepted, and that person's prayer will reach to the clouds.

35:16 The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds, and it will not rest until it reaches its goal; it will not desist until the Most High responds

35:17 and does right by the righteous and executes judgment. The Lord will not delay, nor will he be slow on their behalf,

35:18 until he crushes the loins of the merciless and repays the nations with vengeance; until he sweeps away the multitude of the arrogant and breaks the scepters of the unrighteous;

35:19 until he repays every person according to their deeds, and human works according to their intentions; until he vindicates the cause of his people and makes them rejoice in his mercy.

35:20 Mercy is as welcome in a time of distress as rain clouds in a time of drought.
